div.head: Rect 20, 20.1, 20.2
div.ab: [20] Hæigwerde gebyreð, þæt man his geswinces lean gecnawe on ðam endum, ðe to etenlæse licgan; forðam he mæig wenan, gyf he þæt ær forgymð, þæt him man . . . [20.1] . . . . . . . . . . hwilces landsticces geann, þæt sceal beon mid folcrihte nyhst etenlæse; forðam gyf he for slæwðe his hlafordes forgymð, ne bið his agnum wel geborgen, gif hit bið ðus funden. [20.2] Gyf he ðonne eal wel gefriðað, he healdan sceal, ðonne bið he godes leanes ful wel wyrðe.

Heiwardo pertinet, ut merces laboris eius compensetur in eam partem segetis, que pascuis ádiacet; quia scire debet, si minus hoc seruabit, dampnum segetis imputabitur illi. [20.1] Et si aliqua terrę portiuncula permittatur ei, secundum ius publicum debet esse uicina compascuis, ut, si per desidiam eius seges infestabitur, a suo primitus expetetur.

Hæigwerde gebyreð þæt man his geswinces lean gecnawe on ðam en|dum ðe to etenlæse licgan forðam he mæig || wenan gyf he þæt ær forgymð þæt him man hwil|ces landsticces geann þæt sceal beon mid folc|rihte nyhst etenlæse forðam gyf he for slæwðe his hlafordes forgymð ne bið his ag|num wel geborgen gif hit bið ðus funden . gyf he ðonne eal wel gefriðað he healdan sceal ðonne bið he godes leanes ful wel wyrðe .

Hæigwerde gebyreð þæt man his geswinces lean gecnawe on ðam endum ðe to etenlæse licgan, forðam he mæig wenan, gyf he þæt ær forgymð, þæt him man dampnum segetis imputabitur. [20.1] Hwilces landsticces geann, þæt sceal beon mid folcrihte nyhst etenlæse forðam gyf he for slæwðe his hlafordes forgymð, ne bið his agnum wel geborgen gif hit bið ðus funden. [20.2] Gyf he ðonne eal wel gefriðað he healdan sceal, ðonne bið he godes leanes ful wel wyrðe.

Dem Gehegewart gebührt, dass seiner Mühe Lohn anerkannt werde an dén Enden, die an der Weide liegen; denn er darf erwarten, wenn er dies nicht erst schützt, dass man ihm (den Flurschaden zur Last legen wird. [20.1] Also wenn man ihm fehlt B) ein Stück Land gewährt, soll dies gemeinrechtlich nächst der Weide liegen; denn wenn er aus Trägheit nicht seines Gutsherrn achtet, ist er für sein Eigen nicht sicher geborgen, wenn es, wie besagt, befunden worden ist. [20.2] Wenn er dagegen alles wohl schützt, was er hüten soll, dann ist er recht wohl guter Belohnung werth.

[20] To the hayward is due that the reward of his labour be recognised [paid by acres next to the pasture, which straying cattle first endanger] at those ends [of the fields] that lie beside the pasture; for he may expect, if he does not first protect this, that [the lord] (will lay the damage to the crops at his door. [20.1] So if [the lord] — lacking in B) grants him a piece of land, it shall by common law lie next to the pasture; for if through sloth he neglects his lord's [interest], his own is not safely protected, if it is found [assigned next to the pasture] as said. [20.2] If, on the other hand, he protects well everything he should guard, then he is fully worthy of a good reward.

To the hedge-warden it is fitting that one knows that his labour’s reward [be] on the [field] ends which lie [closest] to the common pasture; because he can expect that if he first neglects that, that one [will hold] him [responsible] for whatsoever damage to the land. That [land which] is granted [to him] should be, by folk-custom, nearest to the common pasture, because if he should neglect his lord’s [land] out of laziness, [then] his own [land] will not be well-protected [either], if it is located thus. If, when all that he must tend is well-looked after, then he is fully well-worth a good reward.

For the person appointed to oversee the hedges and fields, it is appropriate that the reward for his efforts be understood to lie at the ends of the field alongside the common pasture, because if he first neglects that, he can expect to be held responsible for any damage to the land. [20.1] Whichever plot of land is allotted to him should be, according to the common law, closest to the common pasture, for if he neglects his lord’s land out of laziness, his own will not be well protected if thus located. [20.2] Yet if he guards well all that he must protect, then he will be entirely worthy of a good reward.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 20–20.2. B skips a line here, according to the Quadripartitus (ending, like the previous line, with ‘him man’); the archetype began 20.1 with ‘⁊ gif him man’; Liebermann supplies the sense from the Quadripartitus (printed in bold). In 20.2 the omission of the relative pronoun (‘he healdan sceal’) was still rare then; or the original read ‘-ðað þæt’. The Quadripartitus lacks 20.2. K: spacing corrected.; AU: corrected against Rabin p. 330 / 331, October 2026 (was “Hæigwerde gebyreð þæt man his geswinces lean gecnawe on ðam endum ðe to etenlæse licgan, forðam he mæig wenan, gyf he þæt ær forgymð, þæt him man dampnum segetis imputabitur. [20.1] Hwilces landsticces geann, þæt sceal beon mid folcrihte nyhst etenlæse forðam gyf he for slæwðe his hlafordes forgymð, ne bið his agnum wel geborgen gif hit bið ðus funden. [20.2] Gyf he ðonne eal wel gefriðað he healdan sceal, ðonne bið he godes leanes ful wel wyrðe.”, now “Hæigwerde gebyreð þæt man his geswinces lean gecnawe on ðam endum ðe to etenlæse licgan, forðam he mæig wenan, gyf he þæt ær forgymð, þæt him man dampnum segetis imputabitur. [20.2] Gyf he ðonne eal wel gefriðað he healdan sceal, ðonne bið he godes leanes ful wel wyrðe. (expanded letters in italics: dampnum segetis imputabitur)”); AY: corrected against Rabin p. 330 / 331, October 2026 (was “|”, now “∅”)

This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (20, 20.1, 20.2), each marked with its number.
held responsible . . . land: Though necessary grammatically, these words are omitted from the Old English. The text has been supplied from the post-Conquest Latin compilation Quadripartitus.
